message.content:
**The Thinker (Le Penseur) – Auguste Rodin (1880–1902)**  

Rodin’s bronze “The Thinker” is arguably the single most iconic sculpture of the 19th century. Created in the early 1880s and first exhibited in 1884, it captured the era’s fascination with modernism, psychological depth, and the power of the human form. Its dramatic pose—an adult male hunched over in deep contemplation—has become a universal symbol of intellectual effort and has been reproduced in countless editions, casts, and even digital renderings worldwide.

While other 19th‑century masterpieces such as **The Kiss** (also by Rodin, 1882), **The Gates of Hell** (a monumental series, 1880–1917), and **The Statue of Liberty** (a monumental sculpture, 1886) are also highly celebrated, “The Thinker” stands out for its enduring cultural resonance and its status as a shorthand for the very idea of sculpture itself.
